<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec (when written): `SPEC.md`.

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or issues.
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission". Reasoning effort per role is set in `SPEC.md`.
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

64→## 2. Mission setup
65→
66→**Command** (run by the owner from the repository root on a checkout of `main` that contains this
67→approved spec; the mission creates `mission/observatory-v1` from it):
68→
69→```sh
70→droid exec --mission --auto high \
71→  --model claude-fable-5.1          --reasoning-effort high \
72→  --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5  --worker-reasoning-effort high \
73→  --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 --validator-reasoning-effort high \
74→  --output-format text \
75→  -f SPEC.md
76→```
77→
78→| Flag | Value | Reason |
79→|---|---|---|
80→| `--mission --auto high` | required | Missions auto-approve proposals and need `--auto high` (Droid 0.247.0 `droid exec --help`). The hooks in `.factory/hooks.json` are the guard, not the prompt. |
81→| `--model` | `claude-fable-5.1` | Orchestrator (D-006, corrected 2026-10-22 from the misspelt `claude-fable-5-1`, which fell back to GPT-6 Sol). Factory catalog id, 4× multiplier. |
82→| `--reasoning-effort` | `high` | Fable's default; planning and integration are where judgment is bought. `xhigh`/`max` on a 4× model is not justified before a measured need. |
83→| `--worker-model` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Workers (D-006). 0.8× multiplier. Catalog id per docs.factory.com/models; `droid exec --help` on this machine lists `claude-sonnet-5` but not `claude-sonnet-5-5`; the owner confirms availability before the mission starts (open question). |
84→| `--worker-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Owner decision 2026-10-22: the model default; Rust compile errors and Leptos (little training data, PRD §12) need the reasoning. The cost/quality split lane 9 measures is between models, not efforts. |
85→| `--validator-model` | `claude-opus-5-5` | Validators, scrutiny and user testing (D-006). 1.6× multiplier. |
86→| `--validator-reasoning-effort` | `high` | Above Opus's default `medium`: validation is where correctness is bought (D-006 alternatives). |
87→| `--output-format` | `text` | The terminal is for the human; the dataset is the session JSONL under `~/.factory/sessions/`, which attach and replay read. |
88→| `-f SPEC.md` | this file | The mission plans from the approved spec (template, last paragraph). |
89→
90→The same values are declared in `.factory/settings.json` so that a mission started from the
91→Factory App uses them: `missionOrchestratorModel`, `missionOrchestratorReasoningEffort`,
92→`missionModelSettings.workerModel`, `.workerReasoningEffort`, `.validationWorkerModel`,
93→`.validationWorkerReasoningEffort`. The three reasoning-effort keys are added with the spec PR
94→(§8). A change to any model is a decision file (rule 19).
95→
96→**Mission branch.** `mission/observatory-v1`, created from `main` at the commit that contains this
97→approved spec. One pull request `mission/observatory-v1` → `main` at the end of the mission, opened
98→by the orchestrator, merged by the human after `gate` is green. Nothing else reaches `main`
99→(rule 12). The branch is deleted at the merge (PRD §2).
100→
101→**Worktree policy.** One worktree per milestone: `git worktree add ../observatory-wt/<m> -b wt/<m>
102→mission/observatory-v1` where `<m>` is `s`, `m0` … `m5`. Workers and validators of a milestone
103→work only inside its worktree. Two worktrees never edit the same file (rule 13); the shared files
104→(`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`, `docs/decisions/README.md`, `reports/`) are written by
105→the orchestrator on the mission branch at integration. Integration is `git merge --no-ff wt/<m>`
106→into `mission/observatory-v1` by the orchestrator, then `make check` locally, then the
107→`mission-checks` run on the push must be green before the next milestone starts. A worktree is
108→removed after integration; its branch stays (history).
109→
110→**Gate command.** `make check` is the only local gate: it is exactly what `mission-branch.yml`
111→runs (rule 5). A worker hands off only with `make check` green in its worktree; the orchestrator
112→integrates only with `make check` green on the mission branch.
113→
114→**Hooks that must be active.** `.factory/hooks.json`: `guard-git.sh` (PreToolUse on `Execute`,
115→blocks amend/reset/rebase/stash/force-push/push-to-main) and `log-tool-call.sh` (PostToolUse,
116→appends one JSON line per tool call to `build-log/<UTC-day>/<session>.jsonl`). Git hooks via
117→`make hooks` (`core.hooksPath=.githooks`): `pre-commit` (gitleaks on staged files, file size, debt
118→markers, decisions index, rustfmt, markdownlint), `commit-msg` (subject ≤ 72 chars, no WIP/fixup),
119→`pre-push` (no `main`, no non-fast-forward). A worker that finds a hook missing stops and reports;
120→it never disables or bypasses one (`--no-verify` is a rule 12 violation).
121→
122→**Usage budget per milestone.** Unit: USD-equivalent at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, computed
123→from the token counts Factory reports for the mission's sessions (the usage page or the stream's
124→`usage.reported`), pasted into `reports/usage/<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 7). Factory
125→Standard Credits are recorded next to it when visible. The caps below are the owner's planning
126→numbers, not measurements; this is the first mission and there is no prior run to calibrate on.
127→
128→| Milestone | Cap (USD-eq) | Reason for the size |
129→|---|---|---|
130→| S  walking skeleton | 40 | Thin slice, few files, mostly scaffolding and one fixture. |
131→| M0 capture and mapping | 60 | Mapper plus golden tests; the capture already exists (§3 M0). |
132→| M1 board, replay, attach | 150 | Largest UI milestone and the Leptos go/no-go; rework budget inside. |
133→| M2 host | 80 | RPC adapter plus launch screen; the control channel is new ground. |
134→| M3 intervention | 60 | Lane-7 semantics over M2 controls; small surface. |
135→| M4 branch, gate, fix loop | 120 | Two adapters (git, GitHub), the demo branch pair, a live PR loop. |
136→| M5 time, waste, cost | 120 | The metric engine and its oracle test; export; charts. |
137→| Total | 630 | Hard stop for the mission; the final PR and fixes come out of the unspent remainder. |
138→
139→At a cap the orchestrator stops dispatching, writes the usage so far to `reports/usage/`, raises
140→the stall flag and waits for the human (rule 15). Spending beyond a cap is a deviation (rule 9).
141→
142→**What the human will answer mid-mission.** Only at a milestone boundary or when the stall flag is
143→up (rule 15): the M1 go/no-go (PRD §12), a budget cap reached, a proposed deviation from this spec
144→with its reason and cost, a keychain item or GitHub permission the mission cannot create itself
145→(§3 M4, §5.9), the reference spreadsheet for M5 (B-008), and a red `gate` on the final PR.
146→
147→**What the human will not answer.** Style, naming, crate choice within §4, test structure, how to
148→split a milestone into features, which worker does what, or anything already decided here or in
149→`docs/decisions/`. Those go to the backlog with a reason or into a decision file (rules 13, 14).

151→## 3. Milestones
152→
153→Seven milestones on the board of the build: the walking skeleton `S` first (rule 2), then
154→`M0`–`M5` in PRD §13 order. PRD §13 counts six; the seventh is the skeleton rule 2 requires, so
155→the PRD count is superseded here (rule 8). A milestone is integrated into the mission branch, never
156→shipped. The spec itself is not a milestone: it is approved before the mission starts.
157→
158→**B-010 settled: skeleton before M0, and the capture is this mission.** Rule 2 wants the thinnest
159→end-to-end slice first; PRD §13 wants M0 to freeze the mapping before M1–M5 are planned in detail.
160→Both hold because the capture needs no extra mission: the moment the owner runs the §2 command, the
161→orchestrator's session JSONL is growing under `~/.factory/sessions/`, and the skeleton's workers
162→and validators add child sessions for every role. `S` replays a snapshot of that file through a
163→mapper that knows nothing yet (every line is `unknown.event`, counted). `M0` snapshots the same
164→sessions again at `S` integration, now with all four roles present, freezes it as the fixture,
165→and drives the unknown count to zero. The optional B-009 pre-capture is not needed; a small
166→sample-repo mission (PRD §13 M0) is the fallback only if role identification cannot be established
167→from this mission's own files.
168→
169→**Common to every milestone.**
170→
171→- Tests first (rule 1): each feature begins with a red test committed in the worktree; the
172→  scrutiny validator checks that the red run exists in the worker's log.
173→- Acceptance commands are the ones in §6 and `make check`; counts are pasted, not estimated.
174→- Exit needs: `make check` green on the mission branch after integration, `mission-checks` green
175→  on the push, zero blocking findings open, §9/§10 rows written, README/BACKLOG/decisions index
176→  updated (rule 16), `reports/usage/<m>.md` and `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` added
177→  (B-015), and no `unknown.event` on the capture if the milestone adds a source (rule 18).
178→- Must not touch: `main`, another milestone's worktree, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision,
179→  the shared files (§2), the ruleset on `main`.
180→- Fixtures: `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl` is the orchestrator session; its child
181→  sessions live in `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.children/<session-id>.jsonl` with the
182→  `.settings.json` beside each. A fixture is committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` on the
183→  directory is clean and a reviewer has read it; raw lines may carry tool output.

384→## 5. Architecture
385→
386→Each decision carries its reason. Numbers come from the PRD and `config/observatory.example.toml`
387→unless a reason says otherwise.
388→
389→### 5.1 Crates and interfaces
390→
391→| Crate / app | Responsibility | Public interface | Reason |
392→|---|---|---|---|
393→| `crates/observatory-core` | ingest, model, mapping, store, metrics, control, telemetry; **no UI dependency, sync, no tokio** | `Source` trait, `Event`, `Store`, `Metrics`, `Control`, `Config` | Testable from fixtures alone; every milestone's logic lives here so the UI can be swapped (PRD §12 go/no-go). |
394→| `crates/observatory-cli` | headless `replay`, `inspect`, `attach --watch`, `metrics --csv` over core | `observatory-cli <cmd>` | Rule 2: the first thing that works; rule 5: what CI runs; the validators' oracle for every milestone. |
395→| `apps/observatory-app` | Tauri 2 shell (`src-tauri`) + Leptos CSR UI (`src`) | Tauri commands and events, serde types imported from core | One language, no bindings drift (PRD §12). Commands are the only boundary the UI crosses, so a TypeScript UI could replace it without touching core. |
396→
397→Tauri commands (M1 onward): `open_replay(path)`, `list_sessions()`, `attach(session_id)`,
398→`event_raw(ptr)`, `host_launch(cfg)`, `host_control(cmd)`, `metrics(scope)`, `gate(mission)`,
399→`merge(pr, target)`, `telemetry_status()`. Events from shell to UI: `events_appended(batch)`,
400→`session_discovered`, `stall_flag`, `gate_changed`. Batches flush every 100 ms (reason: well under
401→the 1 s requirement, avoids one render per line).
402→
403→### 5.2 Canonical event and lane mapping
404→
405→`Event`, `ReworkWindow`, `Lane`, `Role`, `EventKind` as in PRD appendix A; `EventKind` has one
406→variant per PRD §7 kind in `CamelCase` plus `Unknown { raw_type }`. `source: SourcePtr::Jsonl {
407→path, byte_offset, byte_len }` (appendix A has `path, byte_offset`; `byte_len` is added so a line
408→can be read without scanning for the newline) is the only thing the store keeps of a raw line
409→(PRD §11.2: the lane is a view). `mapping_version: MappingVersion` is a second addition to
410→appendix A: every `Event` names the mapper that produced it, so the first Droid upgrade shows as a
411→rising unknown-event count against a known version, never as a silently broken board (owner,
412→entry 23). Mapping is a module `mapping::v1` with a `MappingVersion`
413→selected from the Droid version in the session `.settings.json`; unknown Droid versions use the
414→latest mapping and raise a one-line warning (reason: an old capture must keep replaying, rule 18
415→covers the rest). A mapping version is frozen at M0 and never edited; a later Droid release gets
416→`mapping::v2` and its own fixture. The golden file `fixtures/streams/<capture>.events.json` is the
417→contract of a version.
418→
419→### 5.3 Store schema
420→
421→SQLite via `rusqlite` with the `bundled` feature (reason: core is sync, a desktop index needs no
422→async driver, and bundling removes the system-library dependency from the clean-clone rule).
423→File: `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` (schema version table, migrations forward-only).
424→
425→| Table | Columns (keys) | Note |
426→|---|---|---|
427→| `sessions` | `id`, `path`, `droid_version`, `tag`, `role`, `parent_id`, `mission_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at` | One row per JSONL file; `tag` confirmed in M0 |
428→| `events` | `id`, `session_id`, `mission_id`, `milestone_id`, `feature_id`, `lane`, `kind`, `raw_type`, `mapping_version`, `role`, `model`, `at`, `duration_ms`, `path`, `byte_offset`, `byte_len` | Pointer, never payload |
429→| `usage` | `event_id`, `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, `credits` | From `usage.reported` |
430→| `missions`, `milestones`, `features` | ids, names, `defined_at`, `completed_at`, `state` | Board model |
431→| `rework_windows` | `feature_id`, `opened_by`, `closed_by`, `cause` | PRD §10.2 |
432→| `prs`, `checks`, `attestations`, `reviews` | GitHub ids, state, `observed_at`, `url` | Lane 8 |
433→| `human_actions` | `id`, `kind`, `target`, `at`, `payload_ptr` | Lane 7 |
434→| `prices` | `effective`, `model`, `class`, `per_m`, `source` | Loaded from the dated TOML |
435→| `mapping_versions` | `version`, `droid_version_range`, `frozen_at` | §5.2 |
436→
437→Raw lines are read on demand from `path`+`byte_offset`; if the file moved, the UI says so and
438→shows the pointer (reason: never copy raw lines, PRD §11.2).

440→### 5.4 Ingest adapters behind traits
441→
442→```rust
443→pub trait Source { fn poll(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>>; fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind; }
444→pub trait Forge  { fn pr(&self, branch: &str, target: &str) -> Result<Option<Pr>>;
445→                   fn checks(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Check>>; fn policy(&self, target: &str) -> Result<MergePolicy>;
446→                   fn merge(&self, pr: &Pr, method: MergeMethod) -> Result<Merged>; /* attestations, reviews */ }
447→```
448→
449→`JsonlSource` (attach; replay = the same source at end of file with a clock the scrubber drives),
450→`RpcSource` (host, M2), `GitSource` (M4), `GitHubSource: Forge` (M4). Reason: one adapter for
451→attach and replay removes a whole class of "works in replay, not live" bugs (D-008); the `Forge`
452→trait is the seam for other forges later (PRD §5 non-goal, §11.2).

473→### 5.6 Metric definitions
474→
475→By reference, not restated: time states PRD §10.1, rework windows §10.2, mission overhead §10.3,
476→cycle/waste/bottleneck/fix loops §10.4, cost §10.5. Closed cause lists used by the engine and the
477→exporter: **waste causes** `waiting_human_question`, `waiting_human_permission`, `waiting_merge`,
478→`waiting_validation`, `rework`, `retry_failure`, `idle_queued`, `idle_unscheduled` (8);
479→**rework causes** `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate` (4). Mission overhead is a
480→separate line in the app and is not exported (reason: it belongs to no card and D-010 has no label
481→for it). The CSV export has one row per feature with every §10.4 measure and the price-table date.
482→
483→### 5.7 Telemetry series budget (D-010, B-017)
484→
485→Contract: OTLP `http/protobuf` to `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp`; header
486→value only from the keychain item `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`; resource attributes
487→`service.name=droid-observatory`, `service.version`; labels only from `mission`, `milestone`,
488→`role`, `model`, `cause`; counters and histograms only; one mission exported at a time.
489→
490→| Metric | Instrument | Labels | Cardinality (worst case) | Series |
491→|---|---|---|---|---|
492→| `observatory.mission.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 6 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (6 + `+Inf` + `_sum` + `_count`) | 9 |
493→| `observatory.feature.cycle_seconds` | histogram, 5 buckets | `mission` | 1 × (5 + 3) | 8 |
494→| `observatory.waste_seconds` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 milestones × 8 causes | 64 |
495→| `observatory.rework_windows` | counter | `mission`, `milestone`, `cause` | 8 × 4 | 32 |
496→| `observatory.fix_loops` | counter | `mission`, `milestone` | 8 | 8 |
497→| `observatory.tokens.{input,output,cache_read,cache_write}` | 4 counters | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 3 roles × 4 models = 12 pairs × 4 | 48 |
498→| `observatory.cost_usd` | counter | `mission`, `role`, `model` | 12 | 12 |
499→| `observatory.unknown_events` | counter | `mission` | 1 | 1 |
500→| **Total worst case** | | | | **182** |
501→
502→Expected for this mission (7 milestones, 3 role×model pairs): 9 + 8 + 56 + 28 + 7 + 12 + 3 + 1 =
503→**124**. Both are strictly under 200. Why these shapes: the feature-cycle histogram carries no
504→`milestone` label because a histogram per milestone (7 series each) would cost 56 series for a
505→distribution the app already shows per card; waste and rework keep `milestone` because the budget
506→meter and the waste chart are read per card. Guards: the `milestone` label is bounded by
507→`max_milestone_labels` (the ninth and later milestones of any observed mission export as
508→`milestone="overflow"`); `role` is the closed `Role` enum; `model` beyond four distinct values per
509→mission exports as `model="other"`; the exporter refuses to start if its computed worst case for the
510→configured buckets and limits is not under `[telemetry].max_series`, and the test
511→`exported_series_count_is_under_budget_on_worst_case_labels()` pins the 182. Series of a previous
512→mission stop being written when the export target changes; `mission_switch_min_interval_min` keeps
513→the two sets from overlapping inside Grafana's active-series window. A `service.version` change
514→(release) re-keys the resource once; it is not a steady-state cost. CI telemetry stays deferred
515→(B-002). D-010 sized the shape at up to 6 milestones; this spec uses 8 label values because the
516→skeleton makes seven milestones and one `overflow` value bounds other missions. Still under 200.
517→
518→### 5.8 Runtime limits
519→
520→From §5.5: 64 watched sessions, 512 MB per session file before warnings, 1 MiB tail chunk,
521→100 ms UI batch, 500 ms JSONL poll, 30 s GitHub poll, 15 s metric export, 20 min stall threshold.
522→The UI holds at most the visible window of events; everything else is a store query (reason: a
523→mission can emit tens of thousands of lines; the board must stay at 60 fps on a laptop). The host
524→child process is reaped on window close (M2 test). No network access except GitHub (when a token
525→is present) and the OTLP gateway (when enabled); both are shown in a status bar.
526→
527→### 5.9 Security
528→
529→- Secrets only from the macOS keychain or the environment (rule 4): `droid-observatory/github-token`
530→  or `GITHUB_TOKEN` for lane 8; `droid-observatory/otlp-headers` for telemetry (no environment
531→  fallback in the app, D-010). Never in config, store, logs or the exported telemetry.
532→- Raw JSONL is rendered read-only after the B-006 scrub pass, never uploaded, never copied into the
533→  store (PRD §11.2); rendering read-only and the merge as the one outward write are PRD §11.3.
534→  Fixtures are committed only after gitleaks and a human read (§3).
535→- The one outward write is the merge (FR-G5): confirmation names PR number and target branch;
536→  the app uses the repository's allowed merge method; the action is a lane-7 event.
537→- Telemetry carries no session id, event id, feature id or free text (D-010); the label allow-list
538→  is enforced in code and by test.

540→## 6. Tests
541→
542→Fixtures are captured streams, named and dated (§3). Local = `make check` in a worktree; MB = the
543→`mission-checks` aggregate on `mission/**`; PR = the `gate` aggregate on the final pull request.
544→
545→| Suite | Covers | Where | Command |
546→|---|---|---|---|
547→| Unit (`#[cfg(test)]` next to code) | model, mapping helpers, time-state engine, windows, cost, label allow-list | local, MB, PR | `cargo test --workspace --all-features` |
548→| Fixture replay (`crates/observatory-core/tests/replay_*.rs`, `mapping.rs`) | each fixture → golden lane events, `unknown events: 0` on frozen captures | local, MB, PR | `make replay-fixtures`; `cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` |
549→| Attach latency (`tests/attach_latency.rs`) | harness appends a fixture line by line; event visible to the store within 1 s | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test attach_latency` |
550→| CLI (`crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs`) | exit codes, `unknown events: N` line, `inspect` prints the exact raw line | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-cli` |
551→| Metrics oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, M5) | engine output vs `reports/reference/*.csv` within tolerance | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` |
552→| Telemetry budget (M5) | worst-case series count = 182 < 200; labels outside the set rejected | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
553→| UI logic | view-model functions (card position, filters, scrubber) live in core and are unit-tested there; the Leptos layer holds no logic worth a wasm test runner (reason: `wasm-bindgen-test` adds a toolchain step for little coverage) | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
554→| Interactive QA (validators) | board, Details, tray, filters, scrubber in the **browser host** `trunk serve --port 3141` with the fixture opened through the file picker; attach, host, controls and gate in the **Tauri window** (`make app-dev`) with screenshots and the CLI as oracle | per milestone, by the user-testing validator | `make app-dev`; `trunk serve --port 3141` |
555→| Coverage (B-005) | `observatory-core` lines | S: reported; **M0 onward: fail under 80 %**; MB and PR | `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` |
556→
557→**B-005 settled: 80 % lines on `observatory-core`.** Reason: core holds every piece of logic that
558→can be wrong silently (mapping, time states, cost), so it is where coverage buys correctness;
559→IO adapters that need a live `droid` or GitHub are in core too and cannot all be exercised in CI,
560→which is the 20 % of room. The CLI is thin and covered by its own tests without a threshold; the
561→UI crate is excluded (wasm target, no logic). Enforced from M0 integration because S has too little
562→code for a percentage to mean anything. Raising it is a backlog item with a reason, lowering it is
563→a decision file.

565→## 7. CI
566→
567→Two workflows, one required check (D-003). Measured per run; the wall time of the aggregate is
568→pasted into `reports/ci/<date>-<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 11).
569→
570→**Mission branch** (`mission-branch.yml`, on push and PR to `mission/**`; aggregate
571→`mission-checks`; budget 3 min warm): markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers,
572→decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`,
573→`make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, plus from S: **`cargo machete`** (B-014) and
574→**`cargo llvm-cov` with the §6 threshold** (B-005). Independent jobs in parallel with the
575→rust-cache. Gates integration: the orchestrator waits for green before the next milestone. If the
576→warm time exceeds 3 min after the coverage job joins, coverage moves to the final PR only, by
577→decision file.
578→
579→**B-014 settled: `cargo-machete`, not `cargo-udeps`.** Reason: machete runs on the stable toolchain
580→in seconds; udeps needs nightly, which is a second toolchain to pin and cache for a check that
581→finds a strict superset only in edge cases. Revisit if machete misses a real unused dependency.
582→
583→**Demo gate** (`demo-gate.yml`, M4, on `pull_request` to `demo/base`): one job that fails when the
584→label `demo:red` is present. Required by the `demo-gate` ruleset on `demo/base` only. Never touches
585→`main`.
586→
587→**Final pull request** (`gate.yml`, on PR to `main`; aggregate `gate`, the only check the `main`
588→ruleset requires): everything above plus Semgrep (SARIF to code scanning), Trivy filesystem scan of
589→the repository (vuln, misconfig, secret; HIGH and CRITICAL; `Cargo.lock` is what makes the vuln
590→scan meaningful), Checkov on the workflows, SBOM (`syft`), the macOS Tauri bundle (`bundle.yml`)
591→with build provenance (`attest-build-provenance`) and cosign signatures, Trivy results and SBOM
592→attached as artifacts. It never deploys. `release.yml` on `v*` tags pushed by the human to a
593→commit on `main` reuses `bundle.yml` and, from S onward, checks the workspace version against the
594→tag (B-016, wired in S; D-009).

3→The rules this project inherits, adapted for a build run as a Factory Mission (orchestrator, workers, validators) with the human as owner. Derived from the artstudio set (14-oct-2026); rules that only made sense for a hand-run team are struck, not deleted, so the decision is visible.

21→17. **Everything is logged.** Hooks record every tool call to `build-log/`; every session transcript is linked from the session log; usage per model and per milestone is recorded. The build of the observatory is itself a dataset for the observatory.
22→18. **Unknown is surfaced, never dropped.** An event the mapper does not recognise is counted and shown; a milestone that adds a source ends with zero unknown events on its capture.
23→19. **Models per role are declared.** Orchestrator, worker and validator models are named in the spec and in the mission command; a change of model is a decision file.

## README
1→# droid-observatory
2→
3→A Rust desktop app that watches a Factory Mission build a business feature: which agent is on
4→what, whether each milestone is validated, where time and tokens go, and the one gate that
5→ships it. Lanes are the mission's orchestrated states; cards are milestones; the last lane is
6→the pull request into `main`.
7→
8→**Status:** pre-mission. The repository holds the PRD, the rules, the CI gate and the
9→configuration contract. No application code yet: the walking skeleton is the mission's first
10→integration (ai/RULES.md rule 2). Rust targets in the `Makefile` activate the moment a
11→`Cargo.toml` lands.
12→
13→## What it will show
14→
15→| Lane | Holds |
16→|---|---|
17→| 1 Intent | prompt, spec, acceptance criteria, re-prompts |
18→| 2 Orchestrator | plan, milestones, task assignment, replans |
19→| 3 Workers | one sub-lane per worker: files, tests, commits |
20→| 4 Validators, scrutiny | findings, blocking vs non-blocking, rework |
21→| 5 Validators, user testing | QA scenarios against the built thing |
22→| 6 Integration | worktree landings on `mission/<name>`, fast checks |
23→| 7 Human | approvals, answers, the review, the merge |
24→| 8 Outside | the PR, CI, attestations, deploys |
25→| 9 Time, waste, cost, models | tokens per role, waste by cause, budget |
26→
27→Full definition: [ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md](ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md).
28→
29→## From a clean clone
30→
31→Requirements: the Rust toolchain via [rustup](https://rustup.rs) (version pinned in
32→`rust-toolchain.toml`), and the tools `make doctor` lists.
33→
34→```sh
35→git clone git@github.com:dctellya/droid-observatory.git
36→cd droid-observatory
37→make doctor      # which tools are missing and how to install them
38→make hooks       # enable the git hooks (once)
39→make check       # every light check the mission-branch CI runs
40→```
41→
42→`make help` lists all targets. The same targets run in CI, so a documented command is a
43→command the gate runs.
44→
45→## Commands
46→
47→| Target | What it does | Where it runs |
48→|---|---|---|
49→| `make check` | all light checks below | mission branch, gate |
50→| `make check-docs` | markdownlint on every `.md` | mission branch, gate |
51→| `make check-links` | lychee link check | mission branch, gate |
52→| `make check-workflows` | actionlint | mission branch, gate |
53→| `make check-file-size` | tracked files under 200 KB (fixtures exempt) | mission branch, gate |
54→| `make check-todos` | debt markers must cite `#issue` or `B-nnn` | mission branch, gate |
55→| `make check-decisions-index` | `docs/decisions/README.md` is generated and current | mission branch, gate |
56→| `make check-secrets` | gitleaks over the repository | mission branch, gate |
57→| `make fmt-check` / `make lint` / `make test` / `make deny` | rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, cargo-deny | once `Cargo.toml` exists |
58→| `make replay-fixtures` | every `fixtures/streams/*.jsonl` through `observatory-cli replay` | once fixtures exist |
59→| `make app-dev` / `make app-build` | Tauri dev window / macOS bundle | once the app exists |
60→
61→## Configuration
62→
63→- `config/observatory.example.toml`: every runtime key with its default and reason. Copy to
64→  `~/.droid-observatory/config.toml`.
65→- `config/prices/<date>.toml`: the dated price table that turns tokens into money. Each cost on
66→  the board names the table it used.
67→- `.env.example`: environment variables, including the Grafana Cloud OTLP contract. Secrets go
68→  in the OS keychain on the desktop; the environment is the fallback and what CI uses.
69→
70→## Running it as a mission
71→
72→Models per role (ai/RULES.md rule 19, `.factory/settings.json`, D-006):
73→orchestrator `claude-fable-5.1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`.
74→
75→```sh
76→droid exec --mission --auto high \
77→  --model claude-fable-5.1 \
78→  --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5 \
79→  --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 \
80→  -f SPEC.md
81→```
82→
83→Reasoning effort per role is declared in `SPEC.md` §2. The mission works on
84→`mission/<name>`, one worktree per milestone, and ends in one pull request into `main`.
85→
86→## The gate
87→
88→Two workflows, one required check:
89→
90→- `mission-branch.yml` on `mission/**`: docs, links, workflows, secrets, and (once code
91→  exists) fmt, clippy, tests, replay fixtures, cargo-deny. Aggregate job `mission-checks`.
92→  Budget: three minutes warm.
93→- `gate.yml` on pull requests to `main`: everything above plus Semgrep, Trivy, Checkov on the
94→  workflows, an SBOM, the macOS Tauri bundle (`bundle.yml`) with build provenance and cosign
95→  signatures. Semgrep and Trivy findings are uploaded to GitHub code scanning, which is also
96→  enabled in default setup. Aggregate job `gate`, the only check the `main` ruleset
97→  requires. It never deploys.
98→- `release.yml` on tags `v*` pushed by the human to a commit on `main`: builds the same
99→  bundle and creates the GitHub release with notes generated from PR labels
100→  (`.github/release.yml`, D-009). Runbook: `docs/runbooks/release.md`.
101→
102→Branch rules on `main`: pull request required, `gate` required, no force pushes, no admin
103→bypass, zero required approvals (the human in lane 7 merges by hand, the gate is the review).
104→
105→## Observability
106→
107→Grafana Cloud over OTLP is the telemetry backend (D-004): the app's own traces and metrics,
108→and the lane-9 mission series (`observatory.*`). Off by default; the app works fully offline.
109→Endpoint and credentials come from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` or the keychain, never from the
110→repository.
111→
112→## Repository layout
113→
114→```text
115→ai/            PRD, rules, spec template, session logs (the human-agent record)
116→.factory/      mission model settings, hooks: git guard and tool-call logger
117→.github/       workflows (mission-branch, gate, bundle, release), CODEOWNERS, templates
118→.githooks/     pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push (enable with `make hooks`)
119→.devcontainer/ Linux container with every `make check` tool (core work; the window needs macOS)
120→config/        example config and dated price tables
121→docs/decisions/ one file per decision; README.md is generated
122→docs/runbooks/  red gate, fix cycle, stalled mission, hooks disabled, release
123→build-log/     one JSON line per agent tool call, by day and session
124→reports/       readiness reports, usage and waste per milestone (pasted from the tool)
125→scripts/       the checks the Makefile calls
126→BACKLOG.md     deferred items with their reasons
127→```
128→
129→## Honest time
130→
131→Rule 10: real time and usage per milestone, stated here as the work lands.
132→
133→| Phase | Wall time | Sessions | Notes |
134→|---|---|---|---|
135→| Ideation → PRD v0.2 | ~1 h 40 m | 1 Droid session | two review rounds; log in `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` |
136→| Repo readiness | ~2 h | same session | readiness Level 1 (5/65) → Level 3 (31/65); see `reports/readiness/` |
137→
138→Token usage for these sessions is recorded by Factory, not by this repository yet; the
139→observatory's first job is to make that number visible.
140→
141→## Licence
142→
143→Apache-2.0, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
144→
## fix-cycle
1→# Fix cycle
2→
3→**Symptom:** the mission has ended (orchestrator reported `mission.completed`) but CI on the
4→mission PR is red, or a check turned red after a rerun.
5→
6→The fix is a new cycle on the **same branch and the same PR** (PRD §2, D-001). Nothing is
7→reopened on `main`.
8→
9→## Steps
10→
11→1. Label the PR `fix-cycle`. Read the failing job output (see [red-gate.md](red-gate.md)).
12→2. Write the fix mission file: the affected feature's spec section, the failing check output
13→   pasted verbatim, the mission branch name, and the original session ids
14→   (`~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`). The observatory pre-fills this from M4 onward; until
15→   then copy it by hand.
16→3. Start the fix in the repository checkout on the mission branch:
17→
18→   ```sh
19→   git switch mission/<name>
20→   droid exec --mission --auto high \
21→     --model claude-fable-5.1 --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5 --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 \
22→     -f fix-<name>.md
23→   ```
24→
25→4. The fix commits land on the mission branch as new commits; the PR updates; the gate
26→   reruns. Record the cycle in the session log and in `reports/` (time and tokens pasted
27→   from the tool).
28→5. Merge only when `gate` is green, by the human.
29→
30→## Stop and involve the human when
31→
32→- The failure is in a required check that does not belong to this repository (GitHub
33→  outage, action removed upstream).
34→- The fix would change the spec: propose it with reason and cost first (rule 9).
35→

# Session Log: 2026-10-22

**Project:** droid-observatory
**Repo state at start:** `main` at `c830823` (Initial commit) — only `LICENSE` and `README.md` present.
**Purpose of this log:** Record every interaction in this session, including the mission that follows, so the work is traceable.

---

## Entry 1 — Session setup

**User request**

> I want to log all this session under ai/session/
> Including the later interaction of the mission we are going to embarc

**Context gathered**

- `README.md`: "droid observatory to observe how a Business feature progresses across the build lifecycle and maybe the SDCL"
- No `ai/` directory existed yet.

**Actions taken**

- Created `ai/session/` directory.
- Created this file, `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md`, as the running log.

**Convention going forward**

- Each user message and the resulting actions get a numbered entry (`## Entry N — <title>`).
- Each entry records: the user request (verbatim or summarized), context gathered, actions taken, files changed, and any decisions or open questions.
- The mission, once stated, gets its own section below and is updated as work progresses.

---

## Mission

Build **droid-observatory**: a Rust desktop app that visualizes how features move through a Factory mission's orchestrated states, with validation status, review notes, merge control, human intervention, agent attribution, and flow metrics (cycle time, waste, bottlenecks).

**Current phase:** PRD v0.3 accepted; repository readiness in progress on `chore/repo-readiness`; spec session next.

---

## Entry 2 — Mission stated: ideation phase → PRD

**User request (verbatim)**

> Perfect. We are going to start with an ideation phase, the outcome is a PRD that I will review. The intent is to create a droid-observatory for missions, where I want to see how a feature or features evolve thru the engineering building cicle using the default orchestrated states of a mission as lanes. I want the droid observatory to be a desktop app written in rust (my preference is Tauri 2, but I'm open to options), the observatory should show if the feature has been validated and is red or green, also it should show review notes by clicking a details button and if it requires a human merge give us the capability to merge. Also the observatory should allow for human intervention if a feature is not progressing as expected (although this should be the less of the cases when we are on a mission). It should show which agent is working on it at a given point of time. I want to also meassure cycle time, waste and bottlenecks.

**Requirements extracted**

1. Desktop app in Rust; preferred stack Tauri 2 (open to alternatives).
2. Board view: lanes = default orchestrated states of a Factory mission; cards = features.
3. Per feature: validation status (red/green).
4. Per feature: "Details" button → review notes.
5. Per feature: if human merge required → merge action from the app.
6. Human intervention on stalled / off-track features (expected to be rare).
7. Show which agent is currently working on each feature.
8. Metrics: cycle time, waste, bottlenecks.

**Plan for this phase**

1. Research Factory mission model (states, API/CLI surface) from docs.
2. Clarify open decisions with the user where needed.
3. Draft PRD → `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`.
4. Update this log with decisions and outcome.

**Research findings (Factory docs, local machine)**

- Docs name the mission roles (orchestrator, feature workers, validators: *scrutiny* and *user-testing*, milestones) but do **not** publish named feature states. Lanes must be defined by us.
- Public API: `GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/children` (mission agents + last status + attention), `POST .../interrupt`, `POST .../messages`.
- `droid exec --mission --output-format stream-jsonrpc` exposes a live JSON-RPC event stream (text deltas, tool events, token usage). Richest data; app must host the mission.
- No mission has run on this machine; `~/.factory` has no mission data to inspect. Sessions are stored as `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`.

**Decisions (user, via questionnaire)**

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Data source | Host missions (spawn `droid exec --mission`, consume JSON-RPC stream) **and** read local `~/.factory` session files |
| Lanes | User will provide the exact list of states |
| Merge | Merge = the **gate**: feature PR into `main`, by human or policy, triggering attested CI (and CD if part of an ecosystem). Work inside the mission is integration, not the gate |
| UI stack | Compare options in PRD and recommend one |

---

## Entry 3 — Added requirement: mission cost

**User request (verbatim)**

> Also I would like to meassure cost of the mission, by meassuring token usage per sub-droid

**Requirement added**

9. Cost: measure token usage (and derived cost) per sub-droid (orchestrator, each worker, each validator), aggregated per feature, per milestone, and per mission.

**Open questions still pending**

- Exact ordered list of mission states (lanes).
- How the external merge gate appears on the board (final lane, badge, or both).
- Card granularity (mission feature vs feature PR).

---

## Entry 4 — Final design decisions before PRD draft

**Decisions (user, via questionnaire)**

**Lanes (exact, ordered):**

1. **Intent**: mission prompt, spec, acceptance criteria; later human re-prompts. Few events.
2. **Orchestrator**: plan, feature breakdown, milestones, task assignment, replans.
3. **Workers**: one sub-lane per worker (or per feature when the mission names them); events: task started, files touched, tests run, commits, task done.
4. **Validators, scrutiny**: review findings, blocking vs non-blocking, re-work requested.
5. **Validators, user testing**: QA runs against the built thing, scenario results.
6. **Integration**: worktree merges into the mission branch, conflicts, gate command runs ("integrated in mission", not "merged").
7. **Human**: approvals, answers to escalations, review of the outcome (the video), the merge of the PR.
8. **Outside**: GitHub PR opened, CI runs and attestations, deploys (ecosystem lane; empty for the observatory itself).
9. **Time, Waste, Cost and models**: tokens and usage per role, which model did what; doubles as budget meter; elapsed time, time stuck/wasted.

Every event carries session id, role, model, timestamp, duration, and a link to the raw JSONL line. **The lane is a view, not a copy.** Lanes 1–6 from the stream, 7–8 from GitHub and human actions, 9 from session metadata.

**Waste definition (user):**
- Active time: worker/validator/orchestrator doing something (tool call in flight, model generating).
- Waiting on human: question/approval open, nobody acting (lane 7 open, lanes 2–6 idle).
- Waiting on validation: work done, validator not started.
- Rework: time spent after a blocking finding on the same task.
- Retry and failure: tool errors, re-runs of same command, integration conflicts.
- **Waste = everything that is not active time on first-pass work**, split by cause, per feature and per role. Cost shown next to it (tokens × per-model multiplier) so slow-cheap vs fast-expensive models compare honestly.

**Gate (lane 8 + badge):** final lane holds the gate (PR opened → checks → merged); card badge shows gate state (pending, human required, policy-merged, CI green/red). **CI red reopens the mission**: new mission cycle on the same feature tagged `fix`, drawn as a loop back into Workers lane. Merge button appears only when policy says a human merges; otherwise badge flips to policy-merged automatically. A mission is complete when the gate is green and the merge happened, not when workers stop. Every red is a counted rework loop in lane 9.

**Card:** one card = one mission feature. Gate lane groups cards by the PR that carries them, badge on the group. A PR with three features shows three cards sharing one gate state. CI red loops back only to the card the fix touches.

**Cost:** tokens + Factory Standard Credits if the stream exposes them, else a price table. **Price table lives in a dated config file so every cost on the board names the prices it used.**

**Next:** draft PRD at `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`.

---

## Entry 5 — PRD draft v0.1 written

**Output:** `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` (Draft v0.1 for review).

**Structure:** Summary · Problem · Goals · Non-goals · Users · Lanes (9, with sources and event kinds) · Board model (card = feature, PR grouping at gate, fix loop, completion rule) · Functional requirements (Board, Details, Agent attribution, Human intervention, Merge gate, Metrics, Mission lifecycle) · Metric definitions (time states, cycle, waste, bottleneck, cost + dated price table) · Data sources and architecture (`observatory-core` lib, SQLite index pointing at raw JSONL, GitHub adapter trait) · Technology options (5 compared) · Milestones M0–M5 · Risks · PRD acceptance criteria · Appendix (canonical `Event` struct, glossary).

**Recommendation made:** Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust end-to-end), with Tauri 2 + TypeScript as the documented fallback if the UI becomes the bottleneck. Core logic isolated in `observatory-core` so the frontend can be swapped.

**Key assumptions flagged for review**

- Mission JSON-RPC event schema is not fully documented; M0 is a capture-and-map milestone before any UI.
- Factory Standard Credits may not be exposed per session; price table is the first-class fallback.
- Merge policy read from GitHub branch protection/rulesets plus an app-level override.
- Fix cycle after a finished mission launches a follow-up mission pre-filled with feature spec + failing check output.

**Status:** awaiting user review of the PRD.

---

## Entry 6 — User review of PRD v0.1

**User review notes (verbatim)**

> # Review notes on droid-observatory-prd.md (22-oct-2026)
>
> Hints on the four points raised, plus one model correction that changes sections 7 and 12.
>
> ## 0. Delivery model (overrides my earlier "one milestone = one PR")
>
> - A **mission is a business feature: the unit that ships.** For this project, v1 of the observatory. One PR into `main` at the end, outcome-sized, with the evidence attached; the full attested CI runs on that PR; CD runs from `main`.
> - **Milestones are internal iterations**, not shippable. Each runs in its own worktree and is integrated into a `mission/<name>` branch, the mission's interface to `main`. Fast checks run on that branch (tests, lint, the gate command) to keep it healthy; nothing on it is shippable or pretends to be.
> - The mission branch is short-lived by construction: it dies at the merge. That is what keeps it from becoming git-flow's `dev`.
> - The board agrees with this: cards are milestones (the spec phases); the gate group is the mission's one PR; lane 6 is integration into `mission/<name>`; lane 8 is the PR. The fix loop after CI red reopens the mission on its branch; it does not open a new PR.
> - M0 (stream capture and mapping) is the first milestone of the same mission: the orchestrator captures a run and freezes the mapping before planning the rest. A manual 20-minute capture beforehand is optional insurance, not a structural step.
>
> ## 1. Section 6, event kinds to add
>
> - Lane 1 (Intent): `question.asked` (orchestrator to human), `intent.answered`, `spec.versioned`.
> - Lane 2 (Orchestrator): `milestone.completed`, `task.skipped`, `mission.paused`, `mission.resumed`, `mission.completed`, `context.compacted` (explains sudden quality drops).
> - Lane 3 (Workers): `subagent.spawned`, `subagent.finished`, `permission.requested`, `permission.granted`, `permission.denied`, `hook.blocked` (the write guard), `usage.reported` (feeds lane 9), `model.changed`.
> - Lane 4 (Scrutiny): `rework.resolved`, the closing event that bounds a rework window.
> - Lane 6 (Integration): `gate_command.passed` and `gate_command.failed`, not only `run`.
> - Lane 8 (Outside): `pr.review_requested`, `check.required_missing`, `ruleset.blocked`, `attestation.verified` (distinct from `attestation.recorded`).
> - Keep `unknown.event` as a first-class kind, counted and surfaced; M0's exit criterion is driving it to zero on the capture.
>
> ## 2. Section 9.2, metric definitions
>
> - **Rework** as written counts all active time after the first blocking signal, so legitimate new work after a fix reads as waste. Bound it: rework = active time between a blocking signal (`finding.blocking`, `qa.scenario.failed`, `integration.conflict`, `check.failed`) and its resolution event (`rework.resolved`, `qa.scenario.passed`, conflict resolved, `check.passed`), per signal. Overlapping windows merge.
> - **First-pass active time** = active time outside any rework window (not "before the first blocking signal").
> - **Mission overhead**: orchestrator time before `feature.defined` (and replanning time not attributable to one feature) belongs to no card. Report it separately, or apportion it explicitly; otherwise feature cycle times look shorter than the mission.
> - **Waiting on merge**: checks green, policy requires a human, nobody has merged. Add it as its own cause under waiting on human; it will be the largest waste bucket in practice.
> - **Cycle time** stops at `pr.merged` (human or policy) with CI green: correct for the gate.
> - **Idle** should distinguish "queued behind another feature" (WIP limit) from "nothing scheduled"; the first is a bottleneck signal, the second is not.
>
> ## 3. Section 11, stack
>
> - Tauri 2 + Leptos is defensible for the stated needs (markdown and video in Details, shared serde types, live board).
> - Two risks to name: Droids have far less Leptos than React or Svelte in their training, and the WASM/Trunk toolchain inside a Mission is a new failure mode. Mitigations already in the PRD are the right ones (core first, headless `observatory replay`, swap to TypeScript at the Tauri command boundary); make M1 the explicit go/no-go on Leptos, with the criterion written down (board renders replay in under N sessions of rework).
> - Update the model ids in the price-table example: `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7` are old; current ids are `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. Keep the table dated.
>
> ## 4. Section 12, milestones as the mission plan
>
> - The order M0 to M5 is right as the seed of the mission plan, under the delivery model in section 0: one mission, six milestones, one `mission/observatory-v1` branch, one PR at the end.
> - M0 must complete before the orchestrator plans M1 onward in detail: the stream schema is unknown until the capture exists. Plan the rest after M0, from the frozen mapping.
> - M4 (gate and fix loop) needs a repository with a PR flow, CI and rulesets to test against; use a private demo repository with CI rather than the observatory itself, which has no PR flow until the end of the mission.
> - M5's acceptance ("matches a hand-computed reference") needs the reference to exist: a spreadsheet computed by hand from the M0 capture, produced by the human once. Validators cannot invent that oracle.
> - Dogfooding from M1 holds: the mission that builds the observatory is observed in the observatory; its own lane 8 stays empty until the final PR.

**Action:** revise PRD to v0.2 incorporating all points. Card unit changes from feature to milestone; gate becomes the mission's single PR; fix loop reopens the mission on `mission/<name>`, no new PR.

---

## Entry 7 — PRD v0.2 written

**Output:** `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` updated to Draft v0.2. Full change table in the PRD's Appendix C.

**Main changes**

- New section 2 "Delivery model": mission = shippable business feature, one PR into `main`; milestones = internal iterations in worktrees integrated into `mission/<name>` with fast checks; branch dies at merge; fix loop reopens the mission on its branch, same PR.
- Card = milestone (features listed inside; metrics at feature granularity, rolled up). One gate group per mission PR; pre-gate placeholder shows mission branch fast-check status.
- All requested event kinds added to section 7; `unknown.event` first-class with an "unmapped" tray (FR-B7); M0 exit criterion = zero unknown events on the capture.
- Metrics: bounded rework windows (signal → resolution, overlapping merge, unresolved reported); first-pass = active outside any window; mission overhead reported separately; waiting on merge as a sub-cause; idle split into queued (bottleneck signal) vs unscheduled; cycle time at feature/milestone/mission levels.
- Stack: Leptos kept, with the two named risks (training data, WASM/Trunk in a mission) and an M1 go/no-go criterion: replay renders with ≤ 3 worker sessions of rework after first scrutiny and a clean-checkout Trunk build; otherwise switch to TypeScript at the Tauri boundary. Threshold 3 flagged as a proposal.
- Price table example re-dated 2026-10-22 with current model ids (`claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`), values left as placeholders.
- Milestones: one mission on `mission/observatory-v1`; M0 is the planning gate; M4 tested on a private demo repo; M5 validated against a human-produced reference spreadsheet listed as a mission input; manual pre-capture noted as optional insurance.
- FR-G rewritten for the mission branch: identify branch/worktrees, fast checks → lane 6, mission PR detection, rule attribution, fix on same branch, completion on merge.
- Appendix A adds `ReworkWindow`; glossary updated.

**Status:** awaiting user review of v0.2.

---

## Entry 8 — v0.2 call-outs accepted

**User:** "agreed on both"

**Confirmed**

1. Cycle time split: feature cycle ends at last `task.done` with validation green and integrated; milestone cycle ends at `milestone.completed`; mission cycle ends at `pr.merged` with CI green.
2. Leptos go/no-go threshold at M1: at most 3 worker sessions of rework after first scrutiny, plus clean-checkout Trunk build. Threshold stands; may be adjusted at planning time.

**Status:** PRD v0.2 open items resolved. Awaiting either full acceptance of v0.2 or further review notes.

---

## Entry 9 — Commit

**User:** "commit is good to go"

**Action:** committed `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` (v0.2) and `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` to `main`.

---

## Entry 10 — Project standards added: `ai/RULES.md` and `ai/SPEC-TEMPLATE.md`

**User:** "add them as well - these are my standards of spec generation and rules that we need to follow"

**Action:** committed both files (user-authored) in a new commit.

**Implications noted for the next phase**

- Next artifact is **`SPEC.md`**, written in an interactive spec session with the PRD, review notes, `RULES.md` and `SPEC-TEMPLATE.md` as inputs, approved by the human before the mission starts. The mission plans from the approved spec; it does not write it.

The PRD's M0 (capture + mapping freeze) and the skeleton overlap; the spec must settle their order and boundary.
- Rule 6 / template §7: CI split already matches the PRD's delivery model (light checks on `mission/<name>`, full attested run on the single PR). Spec must enumerate the tool list from rule 6.
- Rule 12: git forward only, never amend/reset/rebase/stash. Applies to this session too.
- Rules 16–17: README, decisions, backlog, build-log and **this session log** are deliverables extended at every integration; hooks record tool calls to `build-log/`; the build of the observatory is itself a dataset for the observatory.
- Rule 18 matches PRD `unknown.event` handling. Rule 19: models per role declared in spec and mission command; a model change is a decision file.
- Rule 15: human messages the mission only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up. Matches PRD FR-H6.

**Status:** PRD v0.2 and standards committed. Ready for the spec session when the user starts it.

---

## Entry 11 — Agent Readiness Report (baseline, pre-code)

**Trigger:** readiness report run on the repository at commit `56ba6c6` (docs only: README, LICENSE, `ai/`).

**Result:** **Level 1**, 5 of 65 evaluated criteria pass (7.7%); 19 criteria skipped as not applicable (desktop app, no code yet).
